newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tightens security in key northern town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tightens security in key northern town.

text.p: Sri Lanka has tightened security in northern Vavuniya, gateway to the Wanni jungle stronghold of the Tamil Tiger guerrillas, to prevent rebel infiltration, military officials and residents said on Thursday.
"We're trying to flush out (rebel) infiltrators," said a military official in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Residents said they had noted increased army and police checkpoints and patrols to check infiltration by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.
"The numbers of troops have increased," a resident said.

On Monday, two people were killed and 24, mostly civilians, were wounded when a bomb attached to a bicycle exploded in a marketplace in Vavuniya. Police said it was the handiwork of the rebels, but the LTTE have denied the charge.
The rebels, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, could be trying to destabilise Vavuniya, military officials said.

The rebels staged a daring attack on military defences north of Vavuniya last week. Military officials said up to 140 soldiers and 320 rebels were killed in the fighting. The LTTE have said they lost only 50 of their fighters.
The rebels also blew up an ammunition dump and three artillery guns.
Meanwhile, the security forces launched air and artillery strikes on guerrillas in the north and east on Wednesday to disrupt rebel preparations for attacks, military officials said.

Air force jets bombed suspected rebel artillery positions near the town of Puliyankulam, north of Vavuniya, which is the target of troops on Operation "Jaya Sikuru", an offensive into the Wanni, they said.
About 20,000 troops launched Operation Jaya Sikuru, or "Sure of Victory", last month in an attempt to open a highway linking Vavuniya to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The rebels have used artillery captured in earlier raids on army camps to bombard military positions.
The guns have also caused heavy casualties among troops on the offensive into the Wanni.
Military officials in Ampara, 220 km (138 miles) east of Colombo, said army artillery bombarded suspected rebel concentrations in nearby jungles on Wednesday.

"We got intelligence of a terrorist build-up in the Wellaveli and Mandur areas," said a military official. "We shelled the area to disperse the terrorists since they were probably preparing for an attack."
Details of rebel casualties in the air and artillery strikes were not available, military officials said.
The military spokesman said he had no immediate word on the attacks.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year, but the rebels say the toll is higher.
